name: Hippach
kurzbeschreibung: Village community in the middle of the Zillertal, featuring a baroque church and stunning hikes into the Schmirntal.
beschreibung:
Overview

Hippach is situated at an altitude of 608 metres in the upper Zillertal valley within the district of Schwaz, directly neighbouring the renowned alpine destination of Mayrhofen. The vibrant holiday municipality covers almost 40 square kilometres, extending from the sunlit valley floor west of the Ziller River across the steep Schwendberg mountain to alpine heights above 2,700 metres, with a population of around 1,450. Hippach unites the historical communities of Hippach village, Laimach, and Schwendberg, merged in 1973. As a core hub of the Mayrhofen-Hippach holiday region, the village delights guests with authentic Tyrolean folklore, scenic heritage farmsteads, and seamless access to the surrounding Zillertal and Tux Alps.

History

Human settlement here dates back centuries: Laimach was documented around 1150 in donation charters and registered in the 1350 Zillertal land record as Laymaw, denoting clayey loam soil. The Parish Church of Saints Ingenuin and Albuin was first mentioned in 1247; after being damaged by an earthquake, the present Baroque sanctuary was constructed around 1700, retaining its handsome late-Gothic spire. A moment of world cultural significance unfolded in Laimach: The Strasser family lived in the rustic log-cabin farmhouse Strasserhäusl, built in 1714. Working as traveling glove traders, the Strasser siblings sang Silent Night, Holy Night at the 1831 Leipzig Christmas Fair, catapulting the carol to global immortality. The preserved house now operates as a captivating museum.

Getting There

By automobile, motorists travel along the Inntal Motorway A12 to the Wiesing/Zillertal exit, then follow the federal highway B169 past Zell am Ziller straight to Hippach. Train passengers take the ÖBB main line to Jenbach station and transfer to the Zillertalbahn railway, alighting at Ramsau-Hippach station. Frequent local buses connect the station to all hillside hamlets. For motorists, Hippach also marks a primary gateway to the renowned Zillertaler Höhenstraße, a breathtaking alpine toll road ascending through daring switchbacks to elevations exceeding 2,000 metres.

Tips

A pilgrimage to the historic Strasserhäusl museum in Laimach is essential for any visitor wishing to discover how Silent Night conquered the world. Nature enthusiasts should explore the thunderous Laimach Waterfall and the Talbach Waterfall with its scenic family via ferrata. Driving the Zillertaler Höhenstraße panoramic road offers magnificent views over glaciated three-thousand-metre peaks and access to traditional mountain chalets like the Hirschbichlalm. In winter, the state-of-the-art Möslbahn gondola on Hochschwendberg whisks skiers right into the renowned Mountopolis ski area on Mount Penken, while illuminated cross-country trails grace the valley.
